questions.text: An architect assigned all copyright in a building design to a developer. The developer then licensed the design to a competitor without the architect's permission. What rights does the architect have?

options.text: The architect retains economic copyright rights and can sue for ordinary licensing infringement despite the full assignment
The architect retains personal moral rights such as attribution and integrity, but not the assigned economic copyright rights
The architect has no remaining rights of any kind after assignment
The architect retains moral rights only if the assignment agreement repeats them

rationale.a: After a full economic assignment, the architect no longer controls the assigned economic licensing rights unless the agreement limits the assignment.
rationale.c: This ignores moral rights under Sections 193 and 198.
rationale.d: Moral rights arise from statute, not only from contract reservation.
rationale.correct: RA 8293 Section 180 allows copyright assignment and gives the assignee the assigned rights and remedies. Sections 193 and 198 preserve the author's moral rights and make those rights non-assignable and not subject to license. Section 195 allows limited written waiver, but assignment of economic copyright does not assign moral rights.
rationale.takeaway: Economic rights can be assigned; moral rights remain personal to the author.

questions.text: A contractor unknowingly uses architectural plans that later turn out to be infringing copies. Which criminal-penalty statement is most source-safe under RA 8293?

options.text: Strict criminal liability applies automatically even if the contractor had no reason to know the plans were infringing

Do not treat criminal penalties as automatic on these facts; RA 8293 Section 217 requires infringement or aiding/abetting, and possession-type offenses turn on knowing or ought-to-know possession for trade purposes
Criminal liability depends only on whether the building has already been completed
Criminal liability depends only on whether the contractor earned more than PHP 500,000

rationale.a: This ignores the knowledge language in Section 217 possession offenses and overstates strict liability.
rationale.c: Completion status is not the controlling statutory test.
rationale.d: Section 217 considers value/damage in penalty determination, but it does not create this profit threshold.
rationale.correct: RA 8293 Section 217 punishes infringement or aiding and abetting infringement, and separately covers possession by a person who knows or ought to know the article is an infringing copy for sale, hire, distribution for trade, or other prejudicial trade purpose. The question states unknowing use, so a source-safe exam answer avoids automatic strict criminal liability and looks for the Section 217 facts.
rationale.takeaway: Criminal copyright analysis needs the Section 217 facts; civil remedies are a separate question.

questions.text: An architect created a distinctive building design. Five years later, without authorization, another firm constructed an identical building using the same floor plans and facade design. What is the most appropriate civil remedy for the architect to seek?

options.text: A preliminary injunction to stop further infringing use or construction, plus monetary relief subject to RA 8293 proof and damages-limit rules
Automatic criminal prosecution for theft, without needing Section 217 facts
Automatic demolition of the completed building as the ordinary remedy
Damages only; injunctive relief is never available once construction is complete

rationale.b: Criminal penalties require a separate Section 217 analysis.
rationale.c: The local source supports disposal/destruction of infringing copies and devices, but not automatic demolition as the ordinary answer.
rationale.correct: RA 8293 Section 186 covers erection of a building reproducing a protected architectural work. Section 216 includes injunction and damages/profits remedies. Section 226 limits damages recovery after four years from the time the cause of action arose, so the source-safe civil remedy is injunction plus monetary relief subject to proof and timing limits.
rationale.takeaway: Civil remedies under RA 8293 can include injunction and money relief, but damages must respect Section 226.

questions.text: An architect created a design in 1999 and died in 2010. Under RA 8293 Section 213.1, when does copyright protection for this individual-author work expire?

options.text: In 2005 (20 years after creation), which is incorrect as copyright duration is based on the creator's lifetime
In 2035 (25 years after creation), which does not apply as the protection extends beyond the creator's lifetime
In 2060 (50 years after the architect's death)
In 2070 (60 years after the architect's death), which is a common misconception about copyright duration

rationale.b: This uses the applied-art period instead of the individual-author term stated in Section 213.1.
rationale.correct: RA 8293 Section 213.1 protects works under Sections 172 and 173 during the life of the author and for fifty years after death. The architect died in 2010, so protection runs 50 years after death, to 2060. The 1999 creation date does not control the individual-author term.
rationale.takeaway: For individual-author works, calculate from the author's death, not the creation date.

questions.text: An architect's building design was published on an international architecture website without the architect's knowledge or consent. The unauthorized publication has been online for three years, and the architect has now discovered it. Does the length of unauthorized publication eliminate the architect's right to pursue enforcement action?

options.text: Yes, because silence for more than two years automatically waives all copyright remedies
Yes, because publication on a public website is always implied authorization
No, delayed discovery does not automatically eliminate enforcement, but damages must be analyzed under RA 8293 proof and timing limits
Only if the website obtained copies from a former client; otherwise no remedy exists

rationale.a: This invents a two-year waiver rule.
rationale.b: Public website posting is not automatically implied authorization.
rationale.d: The identity of the source may matter factually, but RA 8293 remedies are not limited to former-client leaks.
rationale.correct: RA 8293 Section 177 protects communication/display-type economic rights, and Section 216 provides injunction and damages/profits remedies. Section 226 limits damages recovery after four years from the time the cause of action arose. A three-year unauthorized online use does not automatically eliminate enforcement, but the remedy analysis must stay within RA 8293 proof and timing limits.
rationale.takeaway: Delay does not automatically erase enforcement, but damages timing must be checked.

questions.text: A completed building designed by Architect A was acquired by a new owner who removed the architect's nameplate and attribution signage from the entrance and exterior. The owner also authorized major facade renovation that eliminated several distinctive architectural features. Which moral rights violations has occurred?

options.text: Neither violation applies because attribution and integrity rights never apply after building completion
Removal of attribution implicates the right of attribution; eliminating distinctive features may implicate integrity if the distortion is prejudicial to honor or reputation
Only attribution can ever apply; building modifications can never affect integrity rights
Neither violation applies because real property ownership automatically overrides all moral rights

rationale.a: Section 198 gives moral rights a term beyond completion of the building.
rationale.c: Section 193 includes integrity, not just attribution.
rationale.d: Ownership of the material building does not by itself erase statutory moral rights.
rationale.correct: RA 8293 Section 193 protects attribution and objection to distortion, mutilation, or other modification prejudicial to the author's honor or reputation. Removing credit directly implicates attribution. Major facade changes can implicate integrity when the facts show prejudicial distortion. Section 199 gives moral-rights enforcement remedies.
rationale.takeaway: For integrity, look for prejudicial distortion; for attribution, look for missing or false credit.

questions.text: How long does copyright protection extend for an architectural work created by an individual architect under RA 8293?

options.text: 30 years from the date of creation, unless renewed under special provisions
The lifetime of the architect only, without any posthumous extension
The lifetime of the architect plus 50 years after the architect's death
50 years from the date the building is completed, regardless of subsequent modifications

rationale.d: This measures from completion instead of the author's death.
rationale.correct: RA 8293 Section 213.1 protects works under Sections 172 and 173 during the life of the author and for fifty years after death. The term does not run from building completion or project execution, and it does not end at the author's death.
rationale.takeaway: The individual-author term is life plus 50 years after death.

questions.text: What types of monetary damages may an architect recover in a copyright infringement case under RA 8293?

options.text: Only the cost to record or deposit copyright documents
Actual damages, legal costs and expenses, plus infringer profits, or court-determined just damages in lieu of actual damages and profits
A fixed fee of PHP 100,000 regardless of actual loss or infringer profits
Only the original design fee, with no possible recovery for expenses or infringer profits

rationale.a: Registration, recording, or deposit cost is not the damages measure in Section 216.
rationale.c: Section 216 does not set this fixed fee.
rationale.d: Section 216 is broader than the original design fee.
rationale.correct: RA 8293 Section 216.1(b) allows actual damages, legal costs, other expenses, and profits the infringer made, or in lieu of actual damages and profits, just damages that are not a penalty. Section 226 adds the four-year damages limit. The local source does not support a fixed PHP 250,000 statutory-damages formulation for this item.
rationale.takeaway: Use the Section 216 damages language, and remember the Section 226 timing limit.

questions.text: Can an architect transfer copyright in architectural designs to a developer or client through a written assignment agreement?

options.text: No, copyright can never be assigned by an architect
Yes, copyright may be assigned in whole or in part, and inter vivos assignment requires a written indication of that intention
Only if the Board of Architecture approves the transfer in advance
Only after the building has been completed and occupied

rationale.c: The local RA 8293 assignment text does not require Board approval.
rationale.d: Section 180 does not condition assignment on completion or occupancy.
rationale.correct: RA 8293 Section 180.1 allows copyright to be assigned in whole or in part. Section 180.2 states that copyright is not deemed assigned inter vivos unless there is a written indication of that intention. The statute does not require Board approval or building completion for assignment.
rationale.takeaway: Copyright assignment is allowed, but the written-intention requirement matters.

questions.text: An architectural firm assigned economic copyright in a building design to a developer. Five years later, the architect who created the design wants to claim authorship in professional materials. Which statement is most source-safe under RA 8293?

options.text: The developer owns all moral rights and can stop the architect from ever claiming authorship

The architect-author retains personal moral rights to claim authorship and attribution, while separate reproduction or publication uses may still depend on economic-rights permission or another legal basis
The architect can claim authorship only if the assignment was registered with IPOPHL
Moral rights exist only for three years after assignment

rationale.a: Economic copyright assignment does not assign moral rights.
rationale.c: Moral rights do not depend on IPOPHL registration in the local source.
rationale.d: Section 198 gives moral rights the author's lifetime plus 50 years after death, not three years.
rationale.correct: RA 8293 Section 180 covers assignment of economic copyright. Sections 193 and 198 preserve personal moral rights, including attribution, and make them non-assignable and not subject to license. Section 195 allows only limited written waiver. The source-safe answer separates claiming authorship from reproducing or publishing copies controlled by economic rights.
rationale.takeaway: After economic assignment, the architect-author may still claim moral rights, but copying/publication uses require separate analysis.
